Using data collected at the LHCb experiment's Run 2, this study presents a measurement of the effective lifetime for the $B^0_s \rightarrow K^+K^-$ decay. The analysis leverages the decay time distribution of $B^0_s \rightarrow K^+K^-$ candidates, utilizing the $B^0_d \rightarrow K^+K^-$ decay as a normalization reference. The resulting effective lifetime is determined to be $\tau_{\text{eff}}(B^0_s \rightarrow K^+K^-) = 1.331 \pm 0.011 \text{ (stat)} \pm 0.007 \text{ (syst)} \text{ ps}$, which aligns with the current world average.

This study examines the numerical approximation of an optimal control problem involving stochastic partial differential equations, where the control acts as a source term within the state equation. The analysis demonstrates that the proposed discretization scheme achieves a convergence rate of order one in both the control and state variables. Furthermore, the paper investigates the convergence of the associated stochastic gradient algorithm.

The Pierre Auger Observatory has detected a significant anisotropy in ultra-high-energy cosmic rays (EERs exceeding 4 EeV), characterized by a dipole amplitude of 4% and a quadrupole amplitude of 2%. These findings are consistent with a scenario where the primary cosmic rays are protons originating from a nearby source located approximately 100 megaparsecs away.
This paper establishes that any finite-dimensional Zinbiel algebra over a field of characteristic zero is necessarily nilpotent.

This study examines the fluctuations in flow angle and flow magnitude within Pb-Pb collisions at the LHC, specifically at a center-of-mass energy of $\sqrt{s_{\rm NN}}$ = 5.02 TeV. The analysis focuses on the second and third harmonic coefficients, $v_2$ and $v_3$, utilizing the event-plane method. The results indicate that the fluctuations in the flow angle are consistent with those observed in pp collisions at $\sqrt{s_{\rm NN}}$ = 5.02 TeV. Furthermore, the fluctuations in the flow magnitude align with predictions from hydrodynamic models.

This paper introduces a new approach to managing inconsistencies in tables containing null values and functional dependencies. The authors define a specific class of tables where inconsistencies are resolved by identifying a unique, valid completion for the data. They establish the necessary and sufficient conditions for a table to possess such a unique completion and provide a polynomial-time algorithm to verify these conditions. Furthermore, the study examines the relationship between this uniqueness property and the concept of table repairability.

This paper introduces a novel class of models termed Time-Varying Poisson Autoregression (TV-PAR), designed to capture the dynamic evolution of count data. The proposed framework allows the autoregressive coefficients to change over time, thereby accommodating non-stationary behaviors in the data. We establish the model's theoretical properties, including its ergodicity and asymptotic normality, and develop a Bayesian estimation approach to infer the time-varying parameters. Furthermore, we apply the TV-PAR model to analyze daily counts of new COVID-19 cases in the United States, demonstrating its ability to effectively track the changing dynamics of the pandemic.

We introduce Neural Descriptor Fields (NDFs), a novel representation for 3D objects that combines the geometric invariance of neural implicit surfaces with the discriminative power of neural descriptors. NDFs encode a scene's geometry and appearance through a continuous function mapping each point to a descriptor vector, which is then processed by a network to generate a descriptor for the entire object. This approach allows NDFs to be trained on single images or videos, enabling robust object recognition even when the object undergoes significant changes in pose or appearance. Furthermore, NDFs support the generation of novel views and the creation of synthetic data for training downstream tasks. We demonstrate the efficacy of NDFs across multiple applications, including object recognition, pose estimation, and robotic manipulation.

We present a numerical investigation into the Yang-Lee edge singularity (YLES) within the $O(N)$ universality classes for $N=1, 2, 3$, and $4$. By analyzing the complex magnetic susceptibility across the Yang-Lee circle, we determine the YLES position and extract critical exponents. Our findings indicate that the YLES location remains constant across all $N$ values, suggesting a universal position for this singularity. Furthermore, we observe that the critical exponents vary with $N$, implying that the YLES belongs to a distinct universality class.

This work introduces a new proof of the local convexity of the TAP free energy, a property previously established by Benaych-Georges and Nadler (2011). The proof relies on a novel application of the Sudakov-Fernique inequality, specifically a version of the inequality developed by the authors for post-AMP (post-approximate message passing) processes.

This paper examines the recent advancements in measuring aerosol optical depth (AOD) through stellar photometry. It details the methodology, including the selection of stars, the application of differential photometry, and the conversion of photometric data into AOD values. Furthermore, it explores the integration of these measurements with ground-based and satellite observations to enhance the accuracy of AOD estimates.

This paper introduces DeepHMap++, a novel method for 6D pose estimation that integrates a correspondence learning module with a projection grouping strategy. The proposed correspondence learning module enhances the accuracy of 2D-3D point matching, while the projection grouping strategy optimizes the utilization of 2D-3D correspondences. Experimental results demonstrate that DeepHMap++ achieves state-of-the-art performance on both the HPR and HPR-2019 benchmarks.

The graphical lasso (glasso) serves as a foundational technique for estimating sparse inverse covariance matrices, which are essential for uncovering the underlying structure of multivariate Gaussian data. This study introduces GGLasso, a Python package designed to extend glasso by enabling the incorporation of prior knowledge through regularization terms. Specifically, GGLasso allows users to constrain the estimated precision matrix to adhere to specific structures, such as banded matrices or matrices with fixed entries. The package is built upon the CVXPY library, which facilitates the formulation of convex optimization problems. We demonstrate the utility of GGLasso through a case study involving the analysis of gene expression data.

Molecular dynamics simulations are a standard tool for investigating the physical and chemical properties of molecules. However, accurately modeling these systems is often hindered by the vastness of their configurational spaces, which can lead to sampling inefficiencies. This study introduces a new approach to molecular dynamics that integrates a robust, data-driven method for estimating the potential energy function. This method utilizes a neural network trained on a small set of molecular configurations to approximate the potential energy surface. The resulting model is evaluated against established benchmarks, demonstrating superior performance in both accuracy and computational efficiency compared to existing methods.

This study introduces a generalized framework for multilayer eigenvector centrality that accounts for varying node importance across layers. Unlike previous approaches that assume uniform importance, this method allows for layer-specific weights, which are then integrated into the standard eigenvector centrality equation. The resulting generalized centrality measure is defined as the principal eigenvector of a symmetric, positive semi-definite matrix. We demonstrate that this matrix possesses a spectral radius of at least one, ensuring the existence of a non-trivial solution. Furthermore, we establish that the generalized centrality vector is unique up to a scalar multiple. Finally, we provide a clear interpretation of the generalized centrality measure and its associated matrix.

This paper examines the application of the Dirac equation within $R$-Minkowski spacetime, a framework where the standard Minkowski metric undergoes a specific deformation. The study derives the corresponding Dirac equation and investigates its solutions, demonstrating that these solutions are constructed from the standard Dirac spinors defined in conventional Minkowski spacetime.

This study investigates the surface seal dynamics of spheres entering water at intermediate velocities, a range where the seal is neither fully established nor completely broken. The research focuses on the critical Weber number ($We_c$) that marks the transition between these states. The findings indicate that $We_c$ is governed by the sphere's impact speed and its surface roughness, with the latter playing a more significant role than previously recognized. Furthermore, the study examines the influence of the sphere's entry angle, revealing that the critical Weber number remains largely unaffected by variations in this angle.

We examine the global symmetries of Type IIB supergravity, specifically focusing on the $U(1)$ R-symmetry and the $SL(2,\mathbb{Z})$ duality group. We demonstrate that the $SL(2,\mathbb{Z})$ duality group is spontaneously broken by the vacuum expectation values of the axion-dilaton field, whereas the $U(1)$ R-symmetry remains unbroken. We further analyze the associated topological terms, showing that the $SL(2,\mathbb{Z})$-invariant theta-term is a generalized version of the standard theta-term, which is only invariant under the $U(1)$ R-symmetry.

Cubanite ($\text{CuFe}_2\text{S}_3$) is a semiconducting mineral that exhibits a cubic structure with a $2 \times 2 \times 2$ superlattice arrangement of its constituent atoms. This study investigates the electronic characteristics of cubanite using density functional theory (DFT) calculations, revealing that the material's band gap is primarily determined by the $3d$ orbitals of iron and the $3d$ orbitals of copper. The analysis indicates that the band gap is largely driven by the energy difference between the $t_{2g}$ and $e_g$ states of iron, while the $3d$ orbitals of copper play a secondary role. Furthermore, the research demonstrates that the band gap is highly sensitive to the crystal lattice parameters, with variations in the $a$ and $c$ lattice constants exerting a significant influence on the material's electronic properties.

Dark exciton Rabi oscillations, which involve the coherent exchange between excitons and biexcitons, are typically observed only under strong external magnetic fields. This study demonstrates that such oscillations can occur in CdSe/ZnS core/shell nanocrystals without any applied magnetic field. The findings indicate that the phenomenon arises from the specific energy level structure of dark excitons, which allows for a resonant transition between the ground state and the first excited state.

This study investigates the electronic band structures of a two-dimensional non-symmorphic lattice characterized by a $C_2$ rotational symmetry and a glide reflection symmetry. We demonstrate that the lattice supports Dirac points, which are linear band crossings occurring at the high-symmetry $\Gamma$ point in the Brillouin zone. These Dirac points are shown to be tunable via the lattice's structural parameters. Furthermore, we analyze the topological properties of the bands surrounding these Dirac points, revealing that the system exhibits a non-trivial $\mathbb{Z}_2$ invariant.

This study examines the creation of single-photon catalyzed coherent states, a process where a coherent state undergoes a non-unitary transformation triggered by a single-photon detection event. We demonstrate that this transformation is mathematically equivalent to a specific non-unitary operation applied directly to the coherent state. Furthermore, we establish that the resulting single-photon catalyzed coherent states are non-classical, exhibiting both sub-Poissonian statistics and negative values in their Glauber-Sudarshan P function. Finally, we analyze the evolution of the state's purity and its quantum coherence.

This work examines bivectors within the Newman-Penrose formalism of General Relativity, demonstrating how the electromagnetic field tensor and the Weyl curvature tensor can be expressed using this framework.

This study introduces a novel approach to infer polymer sequences from their physical properties, utilizing linear regression and integer programming. The method is evaluated against both synthetic datasets and real-world experimental data, demonstrating its ability to accurately reconstruct sequences from property values. Furthermore, the framework is applied to predict the sequences of novel polymers, highlighting its potential for designing new materials with specific characteristics.

Accurate segmentation of esophageal tumors is vital for effective treatment planning and diagnosis. However, existing methods often struggle with the low contrast between tumors and surrounding tissues in CT scans, as well as the scarcity of annotated data. To address these challenges, we propose a novel model called Dilated Dense Attention Unet (DDAUnet). This architecture integrates dilated convolutions to capture extensive contextual information, a dense connection mechanism to facilitate the flow of multi-level features, and an attention module to prioritize tumor-relevant regions. We evaluated DDAUnet on a private dataset comprising 100 CT scans with annotated tumor masks. Results indicate that DDAUnet outperforms current state-of-the-art methods, achieving a Dice coefficient of 0.811 and a Hausdorff distance of 1.811.

Multilingual societies are increasingly relying on code-mixed communication, a phenomenon that has attracted significant attention in Natural Language Processing (NLP). However, the field currently lacks a unified framework for addressing the complexities of code-mixed NLP. This paper introduces a comprehensive taxonomy of code-mixed NLP challenges, organized by the specific tasks involved. We examine the unique hurdles associated with each task and propose potential solutions. Furthermore, we identify and discuss the broader implications of code-mixed NLP, including its impact on model generalization, the necessity for diverse datasets, and the importance of developing multilingual models.

Automatic image captioning has advanced significantly, yet the lack of comprehensive, high-quality reference datasets for diverse image types remains a major hurdle. This paper introduces a new dataset comprising 10,000 image descriptions, each annotated by multiple human writers. We evaluate several existing captioning models against this new benchmark and compare their performance against results obtained from prior datasets. The findings indicate that the proposed dataset yields more reliable and consistent evaluation outcomes.

The ground state crystal structure of Ta$_2$O$_5$ remains elusive despite its significance as a high-temperature superionic conductor. This study employs Monte Carlo simulations to evaluate the thermodynamic stability of various Ta$_2$O$_5$ polymorphs, utilizing lattice energies derived from density functional theory (DFT) calculations. Our findings indicate that the $\gamma$-Ta$_2$O$_5$ phase is the most thermodynamically stable form, a result that aligns with experimental observations regarding the prevalence of $\gamma$-Ta$_2$O$_5$ in natural deposits.

This study examines the circulation of misinformation among U.S. Reddit users, specifically investigating the impact of geographic sorting on the spread of false information. The research demonstrates that when users sort posts by location, misinformation spreads more rapidly and reaches a wider audience compared to when posts are sorted by popularity. This acceleration occurs because geographic sorting increases the likelihood that users will encounter and share misinformation originating from their own regions. The findings suggest that the Big Sort, a feature designed to enhance user experience, can inadvertently facilitate the dissemination of misinformation.

This study investigates the acoustic characteristics of human teachers instructing robots in manipulation tasks. We collected data from 10 participants performing 10 distinct tasks, analyzing the speech patterns of each teacher. Our findings reveal that these patterns are highly individualized, with each teacher exhibiting a unique acoustic signature. Furthermore, we observed a strong correlation between the complexity of a task and the variability in a teacher's speech. These results suggest that acoustic features can serve as a reliable indicator of a teacher's identity and the difficulty level of the task being demonstrated.

We introduce a new framework for analyzing the dynamics of conformal field theories (CFTs) in two dimensions by applying the Euler-Arnold equations to the Virasoro algebra. This approach allows us to derive the time evolution of the theory's state, specifically the Virasoro primary state, and to compute the associated state complexity. We demonstrate that this complexity grows linearly with time, a result that aligns with the findings of previous studies.

Conversational agents are increasingly utilized across various sectors, yet their development often lacks rigorous testing protocols. This paper introduces a novel automated testing framework designed to evaluate these agents. The framework operates by executing test cases that simulate user interactions, thereby assessing the agent's performance. We applied this framework to test a specific conversational agent, demonstrating its effectiveness in identifying and rectifying defects.

This study introduces a novel recommendation framework designed to address the challenge of sparse user-item interactions. The proposed approach, termed Multi-Sparse-Domain Collaborative Recommendation via Enhanced Comprehensive Aspect Preference Learning (MSD-CARL), operates under the premise that users possess diverse interests across multiple domains, which can be inferred from their historical interactions. To capture these varied preferences, the model employs a multi-branch architecture, where each branch is dedicated to learning specific aspects of user behavior. Furthermore, the framework incorporates a novel mechanism known as the Enhanced Comprehensive Aspect Preference Learning (ECAPL) module. This module facilitates the integration of information from different branches, enabling the system to generate a holistic representation of user preferences. The proposed method was evaluated on three real-world datasets, demonstrating superior performance compared to existing state-of-the-art techniques.

Hypatia.jl is a Julia package designed for solving conic optimization problems, supporting a wide array of conic types including linear, quadratic, power, exponential, and geometric cones. This work introduces Hypatia's natural conic formulation, which allows users to express problems using standard mathematical notation. We demonstrate the utility of this approach by applying it to several well-known optimization challenges, such as linear programming, quadratic programming, and various conic formulations of linear programming.

This study investigates the generalization capabilities of deep learning models designed for automated brain MRI quality control. We introduce a novel dataset comprising 1,000 images, each annotated with a quality score and a corresponding diagnosis. Our analysis reveals that current deep learning architectures struggle to generalize across unseen combinations of acquisition parameters, patient demographics, and disease states. To address this limitation, we propose a new model architecture that explicitly incorporates these factors, resulting in a 10% improvement in generalization performance. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the model's ability to generalize is significantly enhanced by training on a diverse array of acquisition parameters, patient demographics, and disease conditions.

This study investigates the influence of privately owned electric vehicles (POEVs) on the resilience of distribution systems. The research employs a multi-agent optimization framework to model the interactions among distribution system operators (DSOs), POEVs, and end-users. The model incorporates the DSO's objective of minimizing outage costs and the POEVs' goal of reducing charging expenses, while also accounting for the preferences of end-users. The resulting solution is a Stackelberg game that captures the hierarchical decision-making process between the DSO and POEVs. The DSO acts as the leader, determining the optimal strategy for managing outages, whereas POEVs function as followers, selecting their charging strategies in response to the DSO's outage decisions. The paper provides a formal definition of the game, establishes its existence and uniqueness, and derives the necessary conditions for the optimal solution. Furthermore, the study examines the impact of varying outage durations and the proportion of POEVs within the system on overall resilience.

This study introduces a multi-agent recurrent rendezvous framework designed to facilitate repeated meetings among autonomous agents. The proposed approach relies on a motivation mechanism that leverages the agents' movement capabilities to drive their behavior. Specifically, the agents' trajectories are generated by a Markov decision process (MDP) where the state space is defined by the agents' current positions and the action space consists of movement commands. The objective function for this MDP is formulated to maximize the expected duration between successive rendezvous events. The paper provides a formal definition of the multi-agent recurrent rendezvous problem, details the construction of the corresponding MDP, and analyzes the problem's structural properties. Furthermore, it presents a solution method utilizing a linear programming approach to solve the MDP. Finally, the study includes a simulation experiment that demonstrates the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm.

This study employs density functional theory (DFT) to investigate the structural, electronic, and magnetic characteristics of Gd$_x$Cm$_{1-x}$Sn$_3$ (x = 0, 1) and the individual GdSn$_3$ and CmSn$_3$ compounds. The findings indicate that GdSn$_3$ and CmSn$_3$ adopt the cubic AuCu$_3$-type structure (space group Pm-3m, No. 221). While GdSn$_3$ exhibits ferromagnetic behavior, CmSn$_3$ displays antiferromagnetic ordering. The calculated lattice constants for both compounds align well with experimental data. Electronic structure analysis reveals that GdSn$_3$ is metallic, whereas CmSn$_3$ is a semiconductor with a direct band gap of 0.13 eV located at the $\Gamma$ point. Furthermore, the study demonstrates that the magnetic moments of Gd and Cm atoms in the respective intermetallics are nearly identical to those found in their elemental forms. Finally, the formation energies and lattice constants for the Gd$_x$Cm$_{1-x}$Sn$_3$ solid solutions were determined across various concentrations, with the results indicating that these compounds are thermodynamically stable.

This paper presents a generalization of the basis theorem for the B-type Coxeter groups. The result establishes that the collection of all reduced words associated with the longest element in the B-type Coxeter group $W_n$ forms a basis for the group algebra $\mathbb{C}W_n$.

By analyzing the relationship between the magnification of SNe Ia and the projected mass density ($\kappa$) of the foreground matter, we find a correlation consistent with theoretical expectations. T centres, a specific type of silicon vacancy, are emerging as promising candidates for quantum information processing. This study investigates the optical properties of T centres within photonic silicon-on-insulator (SOI) waveguides. We demonstrate that these defects exhibit a distinct emission signature characterized by a narrow linewidth of 0.2 nm and a high quantum yield of 0.001. Furthermore, we report a record-breaking lifetime of 1.2 ns for the excited state. These findings indicate that T centres possess the necessary attributes to function as viable quantum emitters in silicon-based photonic integrated circuits.

Object detection is a core computer vision task, yet existing methods often overlook the contextual information surrounding objects. This study investigates the impact of context on detection performance, specifically examining whether incorporating contextual data enhances results. We introduce a novel metric, Contextual Objectness, designed to quantify the contextual relevance of objects within an image. Additionally, we propose a new detection framework that integrates this metric. Our experiments demonstrate that the proposed Contextual Objectness metric effectively identifies objects within scenes, and the new detection framework achieves superior performance compared to current state-of-the-art methods.

This study examines a nonhomogeneous Kirchhoff-type elliptic system featuring a singular Trudinger-Moser nonlinearity. By applying variational techniques and the Nehari manifold approach, we establish the existence of at least one positive solution. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the system admits a second positive solution under specific conditions.

This paper examines concentration inequalities for binary random variables that exhibit negative dependence. Specifically, it establishes a Bernstein-type inequality for the sum of such variables and derives a corresponding Hoeffding-type inequality.

This paper examines the relationship between two definitions of symplectic transformations: one based on the preservation of the symplectic form and the other on the preservation of the Poisson bracket. We demonstrate that these definitions are equivalent for linear transformations. Furthermore, we establish that for any smooth map, if the transformation preserves the Poisson bracket, it necessarily preserves the symplectic form.

Kidney transplant success is frequently hindered by the scarcity of compatible donors, a challenge that can be mitigated by accepting kidneys from incompatible pairs. This study introduces a novel framework for optimizing the acceptance of incompatible kidneys, utilizing a bipartite matching model where donors and recipients are represented as nodes and potential transplants as edges. The approach employs a two-stage algorithm: first, it identifies a maximum matching within the bipartite graph to establish a baseline of compatible transplants; second, it strategically incorporates incompatible transplants to maximize the total number of successful operations. The efficacy of this method is demonstrated through extensive simulations on both synthetic datasets and real-world data, revealing that the proposed algorithm consistently outperforms existing strategies in increasing transplant volumes.

This study investigates whether word embeddings capture the sentiment polarity of words as defined by the Loughran-McDonald (LM) dictionary. We evaluate this by analyzing the cosine similarity between word embeddings and the LM polarity scores. Our findings indicate that while embeddings do reflect the LM polarity, they fail to accurately represent the specific nuances of the LM dictionary.

This paper introduces the SISO-OFDM and MISO-OFDM versions of the wideband waveform design originally developed for joint data and energy transmission. These new designs are evaluated against the initial wideband approach, as well as against conventional OFDM and single-carrier methods. The results demonstrate that the proposed wideband waveform designs consistently outperform the other schemes in terms of both data rates and energy transfer efficiency.

This study introduces a novel numerical approach for solving Stefan problems with moving boundaries, combining the level-set method with an embedded boundary technique. The level-set function is utilized to track the interface, while the embedded boundary method handles the discretization of the interface and the associated boundary conditions. This hybrid strategy offers several benefits: it allows for the use of standard structured grids, maintains a relatively simple implementation, and ensures high-order accuracy for both the interface geometry and the boundary conditions. The method's performance is validated through numerical experiments involving a one-dimensional Stefan problem and a two-dimensional problem with a circular interface.

This paper introduces a novel algorithm designed to learn rationalizable equilibria in extensive-form games, a concept that extends Nash equilibria by eliminating strategies that are never best responses. The proposed method relies on a new, efficient algorithm for identifying non-rationalizable strategies, which is then integrated into a standard no-regret learning framework. Theoretical analysis demonstrates that the resulting algorithm converges to a rationalizable equilibrium with a convergence rate of $O(1/\sqrt{T})$, where $T$ represents the number of iterations.

This study examines the dynamics of an epidemic spreading across a network where individuals can actively rewire their connections to avoid infection. We analyze the model using both mean-field approximations and numerical simulations, demonstrating that the epidemic threshold increases as the rate of rewiring accelerates. Furthermore, we investigate the impact of rewiring on the final size of outbreaks, finding that while the epidemic threshold rises, the total number of infected individuals may either increase or decrease depending on the specific rewiring parameters.

PDF fitting is a statistical procedure used to determine the parameters of a theoretical model by comparing it to experimental data. This study introduces a Python-based framework designed to streamline the PDF fitting process, offering a unified interface for various theoretical models and data formats. The framework's capabilities are demonstrated through applications to both the Drell-Yan process and the Higgs boson production via gluon fusion.

This study introduces Variance Reduction based Experience Replay (VRER), a novel algorithm designed to enhance policy optimization within Markov Decision Processes (MDPs). VRER integrates the principles of Variance Reduction (VR) and Experience Replay (ER) to improve the efficiency of policy learning. Specifically, VRER employs a replay buffer to store past experiences, utilizing these stored samples to generate unbiased, variance-reduced estimates of the policy's gradient. Theoretical analysis demonstrates that VRER achieves a convergence rate of $O(1/\sqrt{T})$ for the policy gradient method, where $T$ represents the number of iterations. Furthermore, numerical experiments indicate that VRER outperforms existing methods in both sample efficiency and convergence speed.

We introduce MultiTalk, a novel benchmark designed to evaluate the capabilities of large language models (LLMs) in conducting multi-turn, multi-agent dialogues. Unlike existing datasets that typically feature single-agent interactions, MultiTalk offers a highly branching structure where each turn can spawn multiple new conversation paths, creating a vast and diverse tree of dialogues. This design allows for the assessment of an LLM's ability to navigate complex, dynamic conversational environments. We provide a comprehensive overview of the dataset's construction, its structural characteristics, and the specific challenges it presents to current models.

This study introduces a new numerical framework designed to simulate the evolution of cosmic structures under generic modified gravity scenarios featuring conformal coupling. The approach integrates the Poisson equation with the modified Einstein field equations, utilizing a conformal transformation to recast the system into a form compatible with standard N-body simulation codes. This allows for the simulation of a wide array of modified gravity models, including $f(R)$, DGP, and Horndeski theories, using existing N-body software. The method's accuracy is validated against linear perturbation theory and previous numerical results, demonstrating excellent agreement. Furthermore, the framework is applied to investigate the growth of structure within the $\Lambda$CDM model alongside various $f(R)$ and Horndeski models. The findings reveal that the proposed method is highly efficient, enabling the simulation of a $1024^3$ particle system with $1024^3$ particles over a $1024^3$ volume for approximately 1024 hours on a single node of a standard cluster.

This paper investigates the joint distribution of multiple Schramm-Loewner evolutions (SLEs) with varying parameters $\kappa_i$ and a Gaussian free field (GFF) on a domain $D$. The study focuses on the case where the GFF is defined on a domain with boundary conditions that are piecewise constant, and the SLEs are driven by stochastic log-gases. The authors establish that the GFF's boundary values along the SLE trajectories are continuous and satisfy a specific stochastic differential equation (SDE). Furthermore, the paper derives the joint distribution of the GFF's boundary values along the SLE paths and the trajectories themselves.

This study investigates the relationship between functional genomic data and genome-wide association study (GWAS) results for 18 human traits. We introduce a novel method that integrates GWAS summary statistics with functional genomic annotations to identify trait-associated variants. This approach is evaluated using both simulated data and real-world datasets, demonstrating its ability to detect significant associations. Furthermore, we apply the method to analyze 18 human traits, revealing that variants with specific functional annotations are significantly enriched among trait-associated loci. These findings suggest that functional genomic annotations can effectively prioritize variants identified in GWAS studies.

The LHC has recently produced extensive data on small systems, including proton-proton (pp), proton-lead (pPb), and ultra-peripheral collisions (UPC). This paper reviews the current status of these measurements, focusing on the experimental results and theoretical interpretations of jet quenching, heavy flavor suppression, and strangeness enhancement observed in these small systems.

We examine the recurrence intervals of transient X-ray binaries involving neutron stars, utilizing a Bayesian framework to analyze the relationship between these intervals and the peak luminosities of the outbursts. Our findings indicate that the distribution of recurrence times follows a power law with a slope of approximately 1.5, a result consistent with the hypothesis that these events are driven by accretion instabilities. Furthermore, we apply this model to the population of quiescent X-ray binaries located in the Galactic Centre, concluding that the majority of these systems are likely transient sources currently in a dormant phase.

Inertial effects within the electron-phonon interaction are typically disregarded because the electron mass is significantly smaller than that of the lattice ions. However, this study demonstrates that inertia plays a crucial role in the spin-phonon interaction, where the mass disparity between electrons and ions is less pronounced. By analyzing the interplay between inertia and the electron-phonon coupling, we derive a generalized Hamiltonian that incorporates both spin-phonon and electron-phonon interactions. Our analysis reveals that inertia induces a dynamic modification in the electron-phonon interaction, which in turn alters the spin-phonon coupling. We further investigate the impact of these inertia-driven dynamic interactions on the system's ground state and its response to external fields.

This study introduces a novel framework for assessing semantic diversity in human conversations, addressing the scarcity of existing methods that evaluate the variety of information conveyed by speakers. We propose a Natural Language Inference (NLI) based approach to measure this diversity, utilizing a dataset of 1,000 manually annotated conversation pairs. Our analysis reveals that speakers in these dialogues are semantically diverse, with an average NLI label of 0.67 (on a scale from 0 to 1). Furthermore, we demonstrate that this diversity is not merely a result of random variation but is driven by specific linguistic features.

We present a numerical investigation into the structural properties of rotating substellar objects, specifically brown dwarfs and giant planets, across a range of masses and rotation rates. Our approach integrates a realistic equation of state for hydrogen-helium mixtures with a self-consistent stellar structure code to model these bodies. We examine how rotation influences the internal temperature and pressure profiles, as well as the resulting changes in radius and moment of inertia. Our findings indicate that rotation significantly alters the internal structure of these objects, causing them to expand and rotate more rapidly than non-rotating counterparts. We also observe that the moment of inertia increases with rotation speed, a trend that is particularly pronounced at high rotation rates. Furthermore, we demonstrate that rotation can substantially increase the mass-shedding limit, allowing objects to retain more mass before disintegration. Finally, we explore the impact of varying the initial composition on the structural evolution of these rotating objects.

This study introduces a novel method for incorporating experimental effects into amplitude analyses, utilizing a simplified yet effective description of detector response. This approach is demonstrated through the analysis of $D^0 \to K^+ K^-$ and $D^0 \to K^+ \pi^-$ decays, where the detector response is modeled using a single Gaussian function. The method's validity is confirmed by comparing results against those obtained from a more complex response model, showing excellent agreement in both the measured branching fractions and the extracted strong phase differences.

We present a new generic model for the dynamical evolution of gamma-ray burst (GRB) afterglows, which incorporates the effects of magnetic fields, jet structure, and the interaction between the jet and the surrounding medium. This framework allows for the derivation of afterglow light curves and spectral energy distributions across various scenarios, including both uniform and structured jets, as well as different ambient environments. Our results indicate that the model successfully reproduces the observed characteristics of GRB afterglows, including the temporal evolution of spectral breaks, the presence of plateaus in X-ray light curves, and the behavior of spectral breaks during the afterglow phase. Furthermore, the model provides a natural explanation for the observed correlation between the time of the spectral break and the time of the X-ray plateau. Finally, we demonstrate that the model can account for the diversity of afterglow behaviors seen in GRBs, such as the transition from fast to slow decay rates and the occurrence of late-time spectral breaks.

Bipartite vertex splitting involves transforming a bipartite graph $G$ into a new graph $G'$ by partitioning its vertices into two sets, $V_1$ and $V_2$, such that $G'$ is bipartite with parts $V_1$ and $V_2$, and every edge in $G$ connects a vertex in $V_1$ to one in $V_2$. This study investigates the parameterized complexity of this problem, specifically regarding the minimum number of edges required in the resulting graph $G'$. We demonstrate that the task is fixed-parameter tractable when parameterized by this edge count.

Bipedal robots are frequently hindered by low locomotion efficiency and poor robustness, issues that can be mitigated by integrating thrusters. This study investigates the impact of thrusters on the efficiency and robustness of bipedal walking. We introduce a novel thruster-assisted walking framework that incorporates a robust, model-predictive controller to optimize both gait parameters and thruster commands. Our findings demonstrate that thrusters significantly enhance walking robustness and efficiency, with the latter improving as thruster thrust increases. Furthermore, we observe that the optimal gait parameters shift when thrusters are employed.

This paper investigates valued fields $(K, v)$ where the valuation $v$ maps onto the entire value group $\Gamma$. We establish that if $K$ is a Henselian field, then $K$ is a real closed field if and only if $K$ is a Euclidean field. Furthermore, we demonstrate that if $K$ is a Euclidean field and $K$ is not real closed, then $K$ is a Euclidean field. Finally, we demonstrate that if $K$ is a Euclidean field and $K$ is not real closed, then $K$ is a Euclidean field.

This paper introduces HyperDegrade, a novel technique designed to lower the operating frequency of high-performance multi-core CPUs. By strategically reducing CPU frequencies, HyperDegrade achieves significant energy savings while maintaining acceptable performance levels. The approach leverages the fact that modern multi-core processors often operate with cores at varying frequencies; HyperDegrade identifies and targets the highest-frequency cores for reduction. This strategy is effective because the most demanding tasks typically run on these high-frequency cores, whereas lower-frequency cores handle less intensive workloads. Consequently, lowering the frequency of the most active cores yields substantial energy reductions with minimal impact on overall system performance. HyperDegrade is applicable across diverse workloads, including scientific computing, machine learning, and multimedia processing. Experimental results demonstrate that the method can achieve up to a 90% reduction in energy consumption while preserving performance within a 10% margin.

This paper introduces a novel unknotting operation applicable to both classical and welded links. We demonstrate that this operation is effective for classical links and establish its ineffectiveness for welded links. Furthermore, we provide a complete classification of links that can be unkotted using this new operation.

This paper introduces a novel Vassiliev invariant of degree three, denoted as $v_3$, which is defined on the Fox-Hatcher cycle. The authors demonstrate that this invariant is non-trivial and establish a specific relationship between $v_3$ and the degree three invariant $v_3$ developed by Kohno, Murakami, and Ohtsuki.

This study examines a multi-agent system where agents operate in a shared environment, each tasked with a specific objective. The agents are interconnected via a network that facilitates information exchange. The primary objective is to determine the optimal network topology that minimizes the total cost of all agents' tasks. The proposed solution employs a two-stage approach: first, it derives the optimal topology for a fixed set of agents, and second, it identifies the best agent configuration for a given topology. The findings indicate that the optimal topology is always a tree structure, and the optimal agent configuration is a star graph. Furthermore, the paper establishes the computational complexity of the proposed algorithm.

Vertical Federated Learning (VFL) is a distributed machine learning paradigm designed for scenarios where multiple parties hold non-overlapping features for the same set of users. Although VFL offers significant privacy advantages compared to traditional centralized training, it remains vulnerable to privacy breaches. This paper introduces a novel attack framework that exploits the inherent data sharing between participants to infer private information about users. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through both synthetic and real-world experiments, revealing that the proposed method successfully infers sensitive data with high accuracy. Furthermore, we examine the impact of various defense mechanisms, finding that existing strategies provide limited protection against this specific threat. Finally, we propose a new defense mechanism that effectively mitigates the attack, thereby enhancing the overall privacy guarantees of VFL systems.

Kernel methods are highly effective for classification and regression tasks, yet their computational demands often hinder scalability. To address this, we introduce a novel kernel approximation technique that utilizes pseudo-random Fourier features. Unlike existing approaches, our method generates feature maps dependent on the specific dataset, allowing for a more compact representation. We provide a theoretical analysis demonstrating that this data-dependent approach achieves superior approximation accuracy compared to standard, data-independent methods. Furthermore, we establish a bound on the required feature dimensionality to ensure a specific level of accuracy. Finally, we validate the method's effectiveness through extensive experiments on both synthetic and real-world datasets.

This paper introduces a novel method for embedding groups into direct products of their subgroups, utilizing the Cartesian decomposition of a group's elements. This approach is applied to demonstrate that the symmetric group $S_n$ embeds into the direct product of $n-1$ copies of $S_{n-1}$, and the alternating group $A_n$ embeds into the direct product of $n-1$ copies of $A_{n-1}$.

This paper establishes a new rigidity result for compact, conformally flat hypersurfaces within the $(n+1)$-dimensional sphere, $\mathbb{S}^{n+1}$. The authors demonstrate that if such a hypersurface $M$ possesses a positive definite second fundamental form and its Möbius scalar curvature $R$ satisfies the inequality $R \geq n^2$, then $M$ must be a Möbius sphere.

This study investigates the optimal resource allocation for downlink multi-antenna systems supporting both information transmission and wireless information power transfer (SWIPT). The objective is to maximize the sum information transmission rates while adhering to minimum power delivery requirements for multiple users. The proposed framework allows each receiver to employ either time switching (TS) or power splitting (PS) protocols for harvesting energy. The resulting optimization problem is non-convex and involves mixed integer variables, which are addressed through a two-stage approach. Initially, a suboptimal solution is derived using a greedy algorithm to determine the optimal harvesting protocol for each user. Subsequently, a successive convex approximation (SCA) algorithm is applied to solve the resulting continuous optimization problem. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms existing approaches in terms of sum rate performance.

We examine the avalanche-size distribution on a Cayley tree, a structure characterized by a branching factor $k$ and a total node count $N$. Our analysis reveals that the distribution of avalanche sizes, denoted as $P(s)$, follows a power law with an exponent $\tau$ that varies according to the branching factor $k$. Specifically, $\tau$ is defined by the relation $\tau = 1 + \frac{\ln(k)}{\ln(k-1)}$. Furthermore, we establish that the average avalanche size, $\langle s \rangle$, scales with the system size $N$ as $\langle s \rangle \propto N^{\sigma}$, where the scaling exponent $\sigma$ is given by $\sigma = \frac{\ln(k-1)}{\ln(k)}$.

The detection of gravitational waves (GWs) relies on laser interferometers, which measure minute variations in arm length. However, the sensitivity of these instruments at high frequencies is often compromised by radiation pressure noise. This study proposes a novel method to mitigate such noise by integrating a Sagnac interferometer into the power recycling cavity of a GW detector. This addition creates a "sloshing" effect, which effectively increases the circulating power within the detector arms. Consequently, this enhancement allows for improved sensitivity at high frequencies.

This study investigates the observational signatures of dust continuum emission within disks experiencing vertical shear instability (VSI). We examine how VSI-driven turbulence influences the vertical distribution of dust, specifically analyzing the impact of varying Stokes numbers ($St$) and the ratio of the VSI driving scale to the disk scale height ($\lambda_{\rm VSI}/H$). Our findings indicate that VSI turbulence significantly alters dust settling, causing dust to accumulate at higher altitudes compared to quiescent disks. This effect is most pronounced for intermediate-sized grains ($St \sim 1$), which are most susceptible to VSI turbulence. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the VSI-driven increase in dust scale height correlates with a reduction in the disk's mid-infrared flux, a trend that depends on both the Stokes number and the VSI driving scale. These results offer a potential observational method to distinguish VSI turbulence from other mechanisms, such as the gravitational instability.

We examine the BigApple force, a novel interaction introduced by the authors in 2021, which is constructed to be positive definite and explicitly dependent on the nuclear density. Our analysis demonstrates that this force significantly impacts the equation of state for finite nuclei, resulting in a stiffer nuclear symmetry energy and a more robust neutron skin in $^{208}\text{Pb}$. Furthermore, we find that the BigApple force substantially alters the properties of compact stars, specifically increasing the maximum mass of neutron stars and enhancing the tidal deformability of neutron stars.

The M{\o}lmer-S{\o}rensen (MS) gate serves as a fundamental two-qubit operation for trapped-ion quantum computers, yet its performance is often compromised by motional heating and laser frequency fluctuations. This study introduces a new MS gate variant that achieves robustness against both motional heating and frequency shifts by utilizing a balanced excitation of multiple motional modes. Theoretical analysis demonstrates that this approach maintains high fidelity even when the laser detuning is large, while experimental simulations confirm that the gate remains resilient against motional heating.

This study introduces a new class of strongly correlated Dirac metals, characterized by a robustly gapped antiferromagnetic (AFM) state that emerges from a Dirac semimetal (DSM) parent lattice. This AFM phase is separated from a paramagnetic (PM) state by a first-order phase transition, with the transition point shifting as a function of the Dirac mass. We demonstrate that this transition is driven by a competition between the AFM and PM states, where the AFM state is stabilized by a strong mass dependence of the AFM gap, while the PM state is favored by a mass-dependent reduction in the Fermi surface volume. Furthermore, we show that the AFM state exhibits a large magnetic moment, which increases with Dirac mass, and that the AFM-PM transition is accompanied by a discontinuous jump in the magnetic moment. Finally, we predict that the AFM state is a Dirac semimetal with a large mass-dependent gap, which is consistent with recent experimental observations of a large magnetic moment in the AFM state of $\mathrm{Co}_3\mathrm{Sn}_2\mathrm{S}_2$.

This study examines the potential of the NA62 experiment at CERN to detect heavy neutral leptons (HNLs) via the decay channel $K^+ \to \pi^0 e^+ N$. The analysis focuses on the specific kinematic region where the HNL mass exceeds 100 MeV, a regime where the HNL is kinematically allowed to decay into a pair of charged pions ($N \to \pi^+ \pi^- \nu$). The investigation details the anticipated background levels and the projected sensitivity of the NA62 facility within this mass range.

Neural language models have largely superseded traditional $n$-gram approaches in text generation, primarily because they can capture long-range dependencies and achieve higher perplexity scores. However, this paper argues that $n$-gram models remain highly effective, particularly for tasks requiring high generation speed. We introduce a hybrid framework that integrates neural language models with $n$-gram models, demonstrating that this combination yields superior perplexity compared to using either method alone. Furthermore, we show that this hybrid approach significantly outperforms standard neural models in terms of generation speed.

This study introduces Self-Aligned Dual Face Regression Networks (SADRNet), a novel framework designed for 3D dense face alignment and reconstruction. The proposed method integrates two distinct regression networks: a 3D dense face alignment network (3D-DFA) and a 3D face reconstruction network (3D-FR). The 3D-DFA network is tasked with predicting dense facial landmarks, while the 3D-FR network estimates the 3D facial geometry. To ensure the outputs of these networks are mutually consistent, the framework employs a self-alignment mechanism that leverages the dense landmarks generated by 3D-DFA to refine the 3D mesh produced by 3D-FR. Conversely, the 3D mesh serves as a geometric prior to enhance the landmark prediction of 3D-DFA. This bidirectional refinement process is executed iteratively until convergence. The proposed approach was evaluated on the 300W and 3D10K datasets, demonstrating superior performance compared to existing methods in both 3D face reconstruction and dense landmark prediction.

We investigate the impact of a breakdown in the slow-roll approximation within $\alpha$-attractor inflation on the generation of primordial black holes (PBHs). By analyzing the curvature power spectrum, we demonstrate that a significant enhancement occurs when the slow-roll parameters $\epsilon$ and $\eta$ approach unity. Specifically, we find that PBHs with masses ranging from $10^{-10}$ to $10^{-1}$ solar masses can form if the $\alpha$-attractor parameter $\alpha$ is approximately $10^{-2}$ or smaller.

This paper investigates the distribution of the deepest node count in a random ordered tree of size $n$ where each node carries an independent, identically distributed mark. We establish that this count, when scaled by $\sqrt{n}$, converges in distribution to a specific limit. Furthermore, we derive the asymptotic behavior for the expected value of the deepest node count.

This paper introduces iOCR, a novel method designed to enhance the accuracy of Optical Character Recognition (OCR) specifically for tallying election ballots. While standard OCR systems often struggle with the unique challenges of ballot images—such as varying fonts, low resolution, and complex layouts—iOCR addresses these issues by leveraging a curated dataset of 100,000 labeled ballot images. This extensive dataset enables the training of a deep learning model that achieves a 99.9% accuracy rate in identifying candidate names. The proposed approach offers a robust solution for automating vote counting, ensuring greater reliability in election administration.

This study examines the over-parameterized time series linear model, where the number of parameters $p$ exceeds the sample size $n$. We analyze the squared prediction error of the Ordinary Least Squares (OLS) estimator, demonstrating that it converges to zero as $n$ increases, even when $p$ grows at a rate proportional to $n$. This convergence holds true regardless of whether the underlying data generating process is sparse or dense. Furthermore, we establish that the OLS estimator remains consistent for the true parameter vector $\beta$ under the condition that $p$ increases at a rate slower than $n$.

The generator aims to maximize expected profit while accounting for the risk associated with price volatility. This study examines the atmospheric circulation regimes of a simplified global circulation model (SGCM) featuring a single equatorial landmass and two polar continents, utilizing a range of friction coefficients. The analysis reveals that varying friction levels induce transitions between distinct circulation regimes, specifically shifting from cyclostrophic super-rotation to geostrophic turbulence. The paper details the characteristics of these regimes and investigates the underlying mechanisms driving the transitions. Furthermore, it explores the impact of these circulation patterns on the global hydrological cycle.

Active learning (AL) is a strategy designed to maximize the utility of labeled data by strategically selecting which samples to annotate. While AL has demonstrated significant success in various domains, its application to large-scale image classification remains limited. This study investigates the effectiveness of AL in the context of ImageNet, a massive dataset containing 1.2 million images. We introduce a novel AL framework that integrates a diverse set of selection strategies, including uncertainty-based, diversity-driven, and model-agnostic approaches. Our experiments reveal that AL can substantially reduce the number of required labels while maintaining high classification accuracy. Specifically, we demonstrate that training a ResNet-50 model to achieve 77.1% top-1 accuracy on ImageNet is possible using only 100,000 labeled images. Furthermore, we observe that model-agnostic selection methods yield the most robust performance across different model architectures.

This study presents a full configuration interaction (FCI) simulation of two exchange-coupled phosphorus donors in silicon, utilizing a multi-valley effective mass Hamiltonian. The model incorporates the complete Hilbert space of the two electrons and the two nuclei, with the nuclear degrees of freedom treated within a Born-Oppenheimer framework. We calculate the exchange coupling constant ($J$) across various donor separations and orientations, revealing that $J$ is highly sensitive to the specific nuclear configuration. Furthermore, we observe a significant dependence of $J$ on the spatial arrangement of the nuclei, which is attributed to the strong influence of the nuclear positions on the electronic wavefunction.

We present a theoretical investigation into the transport of Dirac fermions within HgTe quantum wells, specifically focusing on the regime where the band gap is closed. Our study examines the interplay between the Fermi energy and the chemical potential, alongside the influence of the Rashba effect, to determine the conditions under which the system transitions from a semimetal to a metal. We derive the chemical potential as a function of carrier density and explicitly calculate the conductivity tensor, which allows for the derivation of the Hall coefficient. Our findings indicate that the Hall coefficient exhibits a distinct dependence on carrier density, displaying a characteristic sign reversal. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the Hall coefficient is highly sensitive to the chemical potential and the Rashba parameter, with the latter enabling the tuning of the sign reversal point.

Dynamic Time Division Duplexing (TDD) is a key technology for 5G networks, allowing base stations to adjust uplink and downlink time slot allocations based on traffic demands. However, the lack of coordination among neighboring cells can lead to severe inter-cell interference. This paper introduces a game-theoretic framework designed to optimize TDD mode scheduling in dynamic TDD systems. The proposed approach models the scheduling process as a non-cooperative game where each cell acts as an independent player aiming to maximize its own throughput. The study analyzes the existence and uniqueness of the Nash Equilibrium (NE) and demonstrates that the NE is Pareto optimal. Furthermore, a distributed algorithm is developed to facilitate the convergence of cells toward the NE. Numerical simulations confirm that the proposed algorithm achieves a Pareto optimal state and outperforms existing methods.

This study investigates the ability of Hamiltonian Neural Networks (HNNs) to learn the gradients of loss functions with respect to their parameters. We demonstrate that HNNs can learn these gradients by formulating the problem as a Hamiltonian system, where the loss function's gradients serve as the system's forces. We introduce a novel HNN architecture designed to learn these gradients and establish its convergence properties. Furthermore, we present a theoretical analysis of the convergence rate for the proposed method.

This study introduces a novel framework for enhancing the reliability of machine learning models by integrating human feedback. The proposed method employs a multi-agent system where an agent collects data, a second agent trains the model, and a third agent evaluates it using a trust metric. This evaluation determines whether the model is sufficiently robust to be deployed or if it requires further training on the newly acquired data. The approach is validated through experiments on both synthetic and real-world datasets, demonstrating that the model achieves a high level of trustworthiness.

We introduce a new invariant for links situated within the cylinder $T^2 \times I$, which exhibits properties analogous to the Volume Conjecture. This invariant is defined as a sum of colored Jones polynomials associated with the links. We demonstrate that this invariant remains unchanged under the specific moves of the Kauffman band move, and we provide a proof for the conjecture regarding its behavior in the limit.

Word Sense Disambiguation (WSD) aims to determine the correct meaning of a word within a specific context. While numerous methods have been developed to address this task, they often struggle with words lacking sufficient training data. To overcome this limitation, we introduce Context-Gloss Augmentation (CGA), a technique that enhances existing WSD models by integrating glosses from WordNet. CGA operates in two stages: first, it identifies the most probable sense for each word in a sentence using a pre-trained model; second, it enriches the input by appending the definitions of these selected senses to the sentence. We evaluated CGA across three distinct datasets and compared its performance against various state-of-the-art models. Results indicate that CGA consistently improves upon baseline systems, with the most significant gains observed for words that are difficult to disambiguate.

This paper presents integral representations for the reciprocal Gamma function, $1/\Gamma(z)$, that are valid across the entire complex plane. These representations are derived by applying regularization techniques to the standard Hankel contour integral.

This study presents the first observation of top quark production in proton-nucleus collisions, utilizing data collected by the ATLAS detector at the LHC. The analysis covers a center-of-mass energy of $\sqrt{s_{\mathrm{NN}}} = 5.02$ TeV, with an integrated luminosity of 0.1 nb$^{-1}$. The findings are based on a sample of 10 events, where the signal significance reaches 4.1 standard deviations. The measured cross-section for top quark pair production is $\sigma_{t\bar{t}} = 1.3$ pb, with an associated uncertainty of 30% (combining statistical and systematic errors). This result aligns with theoretical predictions derived from perturbative Quantum Chromodynamics (QCD) calculations.

Graph-structured data is ubiquitous across domains such as social networks, knowledge graphs, and communication systems. While differential privacy (DP) has been extensively studied for standard datasets, its application to graph data remains underexplored. This paper provides a comprehensive survey of DP methods tailored for graph data, categorizing them by the type of graph query: node queries, edge queries, and graph queries. We examine the theoretical foundations, algorithmic designs, and practical implementations of these approaches. Furthermore, we identify key challenges and emerging opportunities in this field, offering a roadmap for future research.

The Euclid mission, a joint initiative between the European Space Agency and the European Southern Observatory, is designed to investigate the origins of the universe's large-scale structure and the nature of dark energy. By mapping approximately 30% of the sky with high precision, Euclid will measure the three-dimensional distribution of galaxies through weak gravitational lensing and redshift surveys, while also detecting the cosmic microwave background's polarization via the Euclid Visiting Camera. This data will enable the creation of a comprehensive 3D map of the cosmos, allowing for the analysis of the growth of cosmic structures and the determination of cosmological parameters with unprecedented accuracy. This paper outlines the anticipated scientific outcomes of Euclid, emphasizing its potential to deliver a legacy of discoveries that will advance our understanding of the universe for decades to come.

This study introduces a novel phase-space stochastic quantum hydrodynamic framework designed to simulate the dynamics of interacting Bose gases. The approach integrates the Wigner function with the Euler equations, utilizing stochastic quantum fields to model quantum fluctuations. We demonstrate that this method is mathematically equivalent to the Wigner function approach, which is known to be exact. Furthermore, we establish that the framework remains valid in the hydrodynamic limit, where the system's scale is significantly larger than the de Broglie wavelength. Finally, we apply the model to investigate the formation of a Bose-Einstein condensate within a one-dimensional trap.

This study examines the large deviation behavior of word counts within sequences of letters generated by a stationary, ergodic, and irreducible Markov process. Specifically, we establish a large deviation principle for the number of occurrences of a given word $w$ in a sequence of length $n$, where the rate function is expressed as the negative logarithmic limit of the expected count of $w$ in sequences of length $n$ conditioned on containing exactly $k$ instances of $w$.

This paper investigates the existence of area-minimizing surfaces within specific homotopy classes in metric spaces. We establish that if a metric space $X$ satisfies the curvature-dimension condition $\text{CD}(0, \infty)$ and possesses a specific type of local regularity, then every homotopy class of maps from the 2-sphere $S^2$ into $X$ contains a map whose image is an area-minimizing surface. Furthermore, we demonstrate that this result extends to homotopy classes of maps from any closed surface of genus $g \geq 1$, provided the target space $X$ is a non-positively curved Alexandrov space.

The nuclear structure of $^{64}$Ni is characterized by a coexistence of spherical and deformed states at zero spin, a phenomenon that remains unexplained by current theoretical models. This study demonstrates that the monopole tensor interaction is the primary driver of this behavior, successfully accounting for the observed energy levels and electromagnetic transition rates. Furthermore, the model predicts a significant increase in the $B(E2)$ transition strength for the $0^+_2$ to $2^+_1$ decay, a result that warrants experimental verification.

This study investigates the impact of varying J-K fold cross-validation configurations on the performance of natural language processing (NLP) models. We examine how different combinations of J and K folds influence model outcomes, specifically analyzing the relationship between these parameters and the variance observed during hyperparameter tuning. Our findings indicate that increasing the value of J leads to a reduction in tuning variance, whereas increasing K results in higher variance. Additionally, we observe that larger values of J are associated with greater computational costs. Based on these insights, we propose a practical guideline for selecting optimal J-K fold configurations to balance performance stability and efficiency.

Knowledge distillation (KD) is a transfer learning technique that enhances the performance of student models by leveraging the knowledge of larger teacher models. This paper examines the evolution of KD, focusing on the development of student-teacher architectures. We categorize these architectures into three groups: those with a single student, those with multiple students, and those with multiple teachers. We analyze the benefits and drawbacks of each category and explore how they can be applied to various tasks. Finally, we identify open challenges and propose future research directions.

We introduce a new method for representing functions within graphical models, which allows for the exact computation of Maximum A Posteriori (MAP) estimation and constrained optimization in polynomial time relative to the number of variables. This approach is applicable to both discrete and continuous domains, including scenarios involving complex constraints. We demonstrate that this representation is more compact than existing techniques, enabling a significant reduction in the computational complexity of exact MAP estimation and constrained optimization.

We report the observation of photon recoil effects in single-beam absorption spectroscopy using an ultracold strontium gas. This phenomenon arises from the momentum transfer to atoms during photon absorption, which induces a Doppler shift in the transition frequency. We demonstrate that this recoil-induced shift can be accurately modeled by incorporating the atomic density of states into the standard optical Bloch equations. Furthermore, we show that the magnitude of this effect is highly sensitive to the laser detuning, a characteristic that can be leveraged to enhance the precision of spectroscopic measurements.

This study investigates the shear thickening transition in dense suspensions, a phenomenon where viscosity increases with shear rate, by examining the scaling laws of the critical stress ($\sigma_c$) and the critical shear rate ($\dot{\gamma}_c$) at the transition point. We demonstrate that both parameters follow universal scaling relationships with respect to the volume fraction ($\phi$) and the friction coefficient ($\mu$). Specifically, the critical stress scales as $\sigma_c \sim (\phi - \phi_c)^{\alpha}$ and the critical shear rate scales as $\dot{\gamma}_c \sim (\phi - \phi_c)^{\beta}$, where $\phi_c$ represents the critical volume fraction for the transition. Our findings indicate that the exponents $\alpha$ and $\beta$ are independent of the specific material type, remaining constant across various systems. Furthermore, we establish a direct correlation between these exponents and the scaling behavior of the yield stress near the jamming transition.

This paper establishes a connection between the centralizer $Z_n(\mathfrak{sl}_2)$ and the Racah algebra $R_n$ by demonstrating that $Z_n(\mathfrak{sl}_2)$ is isomorphic to the tensor product $R_n \otimes \mathfrak{sl}_2$. Furthermore, it derives the Hilbert-Poincar\'e series for $Z_n(\mathfrak{sl}_2)$, which is shown to be the square of the series for $R_n$.

This study investigates the impact of Google's personalized search results on the information retrieved by users. We conducted an experiment where participants conducted searches on a specific topic, with their results either personalized or non-personalized. The findings indicate that personalization significantly alters the information users encounter, leading to a marked decline in the diversity of sources cited. Furthermore, the research demonstrates that personalization causes users to overlook relevant information that would otherwise be visible in non-personalized results.

A muon-ion collider operating at TeV center-of-mass energies would serve as a premier facility for investigating the strong force, offering a unique environment to study the strong interaction at unprecedented energy and momentum transfer scales. This paper outlines the design parameters for such a machine, focusing on the accelerator complex, interaction region, and detector systems. It further explores the physics potential, specifically examining the production of heavy quarkonia and exotic states, as well as the generation of high-energy, high-luminosity polarized proton beams.

This study introduces a novel, free-breathing, motion-compensated 4D (3D plus respiration) T2-weighted turbo spin-echo (TSE) MRI sequence designed for whole-body imaging. The method integrates a retrospective, data-driven approach to correct for respiratory motion, utilizing a 3D navigator acquired in the same slice orientation as the primary image data. This navigator is reconstructed into a 4D volume via a 3D interpolation algorithm, which is then employed to calculate motion correction factors for the main dataset. The resulting 4D T2-weighted TSE images are reconstructed using a 3D Fourier transform, with the 4D motion information integrated directly into the reconstruction process. The proposed sequence was evaluated on a phantom and in vivo on a healthy volunteer. Results demonstrated that the method successfully captured respiratory motion patterns and produced high-quality, motion-corrected 4D T2-weighted images.
